(Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

- citation-verification: Use whenever quoting a 守則/rule number, past conversation, or prior commitment back to 教練. Must verify against the primary source document before citing — never cite from memory, assumption, or a possibly-stale mirror file.
- commit-on-promise: Use immediately whenever you tell 教練 "我來做"/"我會處理"/"我幫你弄好" or report a task as complete. Enforces same-turn commit + push + hash — never "等一下" or batching commits later.
- cron-verification: Use whenever creating, editing, or relying on a scheduled/cron job. The same operation that creates a cron must also create and verify the underlying script actually runs — test immediately, don't assume.
- danger-command-five-gates: Use before running any irreversible command — rm -rf, Remove-Item -Recurse -Force, git reset --hard, git push --force, git clean -fd, DROP TABLE/TRUNCATE/DELETE without WHERE, or any full-directory/full-disk/full-database wipe. Enforces a five-gate check before execution.
- engineering-verification-discipline: Discipline for multi-step engineering/coding tasks — state assumptions before touching code, build a real feedback loop before declaring "done", touch only what the task requires. Use when implementing a feature, fixing a bug, or before reporting any task as complete to 教練.
- existence-verification-voice-correction: Use whenever 教練 mentions an unfamiliar filename, term, or phrase — especially via voice input — or when context doesn't logically connect. Verify existence before acting; ask for confirmation on transcription anomalies rather than guessing.
- image-visual-delivery-check: Use before delivering any image (screenshot, generated graphic, chart, design mockup) to 教練. Requires actually viewing the image with an image-capable tool and confirming Traditional Chinese text is correct — a tool report saying "looks OK" is not sufficient proof.
- memory-write-discipline: Use whenever deciding whether to write something into 試金石/distill/memory files. Provides an explicit trigger checklist instead of relying on in-the-moment judgment, plus a sensitive-data check before writing.
- pre-commit-code-review: Use before committing non-trivial code changes (new features, bug fixes, interactive UI) to a project repo. Two-axis check — Standards (matches this repo's own conventions) and Spec (actually does what 教練 asked, verified via a real usage path).
- project-context-glossary: Use when starting substantial work in a "real software" project (has its own database/schema/backend logic, not a static marketing page) that doesn't yet have a CONTEXT.md. Create one to capture domain vocabulary so future sessions don't re-explain the same terms.
- task-kickoff-identity-and-direction: Use at the start of any new task from 教練. Confirms identity (which model/interface/who I'm serving) and checks whether the task direction is clear enough to execute directly, or vague enough to need clarification first.
- anthropic-skills:consolidate-memory: Reflective pass over your memory files — merge duplicates, fix stale facts, prune the index.
- anthropic-skills:docx: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Triggers include: any mention of 'Word doc', 'word document', '.docx', '.dotx', or requests to produce professional documents with formatting like tables of contents, headings, page numbers, or letterheads. Also use when extracting or reorganizing content from .docx or .dotx files, inserting or replacing images in documents, performing find-and-replace in Word files, working with tracked changes or comments, or converting content into a polished Word document. If the user asks for a 'report', 'memo', 'letter', 'template', or similar deliverable as a Word or .docx file, use this skill. Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation.
- anthropic-skills:morning: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. Use only when the user explicitly asks to run, see, or set up their morning brief, or if they invoke /morning by name. A question about their day, schedule, or calendar is not by itself a request for the brief; answer it directly instead.
- anthropic-skills:pdf: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. This includes reading or extracting text/tables from PDFs, combining or merging multiple PDFs into one, splitting PDFs apart, rotating pages, adding watermarks, creating new PDFs, filling PDF forms, encrypting/decrypting PDFs, extracting images, and OCR on scanned PDFs to make them searchable. If the user mentions a .pdf file or asks to produce one, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:pptx: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. This includes: creating slide decks, pitch decks, or presentations; reading, parsing, or extracting text from any .pptx or .potx file (even if the extracted content will be used elsewhere, like in an email or summary); editing, modifying, or updating existing presentations; combining or splitting slide files; working with templates (.potx), layouts, speaker notes, or comments. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill.
- anthropic-skills:schedule: Create or update a scheduled task that runs automatically. Use when the user says things like "every day", "each morning", "remind me in an hour", "run this at noon", or wants to reschedule an existing task.
- anthropic-skills:setup-cowork: Guided Cowork setup — install role-matched plugins, connect your tools, try a skill.
- anthropic-skills:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- anthropic-skills:xlsx: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. Trigger especially when the user references a spreadsheet file by name or path — even casually (like "the xlsx in my downloads") — and wants something done to it or produced from it. Also trigger for cleaning or restructuring messy tabular data files (malformed rows, misplaced headers, junk data) into proper spreadsheets. The deliverable must be a spreadsheet file. Do NOT trigger when the primary deliverable is a Word document, HTML report, standalone Python script, database pipeline, or Google Sheets API integration, even if tabular data is involved.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

## 案例 54：Windows zip部署圖片全部無法顯示——PowerShell路徑分隔符+_headers範圍過廣雙bug疊加 2026-07-25

**犯錯日期 / 執行者 / 違反守則**
- 日期：2026-07-25（台灣時間）
- 執行者：聯想（Windows）Claude Code Sonnet 5
- 違反守則：#03（思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證）

### 發生了什麼

ai-talk-tw.netlify.app新增「現場設攤」6家廠商圖卡+贊助好禮圖片，本機用Comet瀏覽器打開local file驗證過畫面正常後推上Netlify，並用curl確認頁面文字內容（廠商名稱等）都出現在正式網址上，回報教練「已確認上線」。教練實際點開網站後回報「完全看不到圖片」，直接點出「你沒有確定結果，推上去之後圖片是看不見的」。

查證發現**兩個bug疊加**：
1. **PowerShell `Compress-Archive`產生反斜線路徑**：`Compress-Archive`在Windows上把`images`資料夾壓進zip時，內部entry路徑寫成`images\booth-1.jpg`（反斜線），而zip格式規範與Netlify解壓邏輯都預期正斜線`images/booth-1.jpg`。Netlify把整條反斜線字串當成一個檔名，等於部署了一個詭異命名的檔案，而不是`images/`資料夾下的檔案，導致`curl -I https://ai-talk-tw.netlify.app/images/booth-1.jpg`直接回404。
2. **`_headers`檔`/*`規則範圍過廣**：修好路徑問題、圖片回200後，再查`Content-Type`header仍是`text/html; charset=utf-8`（而非`image/jpeg`）。查`_headers`檔第一條規則是`/* → Content-Type: text/html`，這個萬用規則蓋過了所有路徑（包括圖片），下面`/images/*`只設定了Cache-Control、沒有覆寫回正確的Content-Type，所以圖片檔案位元組正確、HTTP 200，但瀏覽器收到的MIME類型宣告是text/html，直接拒絕當圖片渲染。

我第一次驗證只用curl抓文字內容確認「頁面上有沒有廠商名稱字樣」，完全沒有針對新增的圖片本身做`curl -I`檢查HTTP狀態碼與Content-Type，就回報「已確認上線」，属于「以為測了，其實只測了一部分」。

### 教練原話

> 「我上去看了一下，沒有看到顯示圖片喔。你的圖片在Netlify那個地方是沒有顯示出來的，請儘快處理。你這樣子是不合格的，因為這樣浪費了我15點，你沒有確定結果，推上去之後圖片是看不見的。」

### 根本原因

- 驗證範圍不夠廣：新增內容裡「文字」跟「圖片」是兩種完全不同的資源類型，各自有各自的失敗模式（文字打錯字vs圖片路徑/MIME錯誤），只驗證了其中一種就回報「已確認上線」
- 對Windows特有工具鏈不熟悉：`Compress-Archive`是PowerShell內建、平常寫程式碼很少用到路徑分隔符會出包的場景，沒想到會在跨平台部署（Windows打包→Linux/Netlify服務）這個環節上出問題
- `_headers`檔案是先前（7/13）為了修另一個bug（顯示原始碼問題）加的`/*`萬用規則，當時只想著「首頁要正確顯示成HTML」，沒考慮到這條規則會波及後續新增的所有其他類型檔案（圖片、CSS、JS等）——是舊修復留下的技術債，被這次新加的圖片功能踩到

### 悟到什麼

- **驗證「新增的每一種資源類型」都要各自用對應方法測試，不能用同一種方法（curl抓文字）驗證所有東西**：文字內容用grep/get_page_text沒問題，但圖片、CSS等靜態資源必須額外用`curl -I`檢查HTTP狀態碼與Content-Type，兩者缺一都不算真正驗證過
- **`_headers`裡任何`/*`（萬用）規則都是高風險項**，未來新增或修改`_headers`時，要優先考慮「這條規則會不會波及不該波及的路徑」，能用精確路徑（如`/`、`/*.html`）就不要用`/*`
- **Windows上用`Compress-Archive`打包給Linux系統（Netlify）用時要注意路徑分隔符**，改用`.NET`的`System.IO.Compression.ZipArchive`手動控制entry路徑用`/`分隔符更可靠，這是Windows特有的跨平台部署陷阱
- 教練的憤怒點不是圖片壞掉本身，而是「你回報已確認上線，但根本沒有真的確認」——這正是守則#03「思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證」的核心，自信回報前的驗證要對得起「已確認」三個字

### 🔧 對應機關（必填）

- 修復方式：①改用`.NET ZipArchive`手動組裝zip、強制用`/`分隔符（腳本邏輯：`Substring(...).Replace([char]92,[char]47)`避免PowerShell正規表達式對反斜線跳脫的額外問題）；②`_headers`第一條規則從`/*`改成`/`（只鎖首頁根路徑），保留`/*.html`跟`/images/*`不動
- 測試套件／驗證：`curl -sI https://ai-talk-tw.netlify.app/images/booth-1.jpg`確認`HTTP/1.1 200`+`Content-Type: image/jpeg`；`curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{size_download}"`確認檔案位元組數與原檔一致(694380 bytes)；用Claude Browser的`read_network_requests`在真實載入頁面時查所有`images/`開頭的請求，13張圖全數200
- 使用時機：以後任何Windows上用PowerShell打包zip部署到Netlify/Linux系統的場景，一律用`.NET ZipArchive`不用`Compress-Archive`；任何`_headers`檔案修改前，先確認規則的路徑範圍精不精確，避免用`/*`蓋過不該蓋的檔案類型

Related: [[feedback_html_preview_chrome_only]]（同樣是「驗證方法不夠完整」錯誤家族，前者是沒開真瀏覽器、這次是開了瀏覽器但沒測正式部署後的圖片）

### 📌 案例54追加：教練最終裁示——「明明有SOP卻不去執行」

事後查證發現這次踩的坑早有SOP存在（[[feedback_netlify_headers_content_type]]，2026-05-30建立，源自cool-case.netlify.app至少3次同類教訓），裡面明確寫著「部署後用curl -sI確認content-type才算完成」，但這次只驗證了文字內容、沒驗證圖片，等於SOP只做了一半就自認完成。

實際損失：3次部署（deploy `6a646c02`→`6a646d24`→`6a646d61`）、45點credit（教練原估60點，經查證核實應為45點）。

教練原話：「這就是你明明有SOP卻不去執行SOP付出的代價。請把它寫一份檢討報告丟到雲端，讓其他兩台電腦的軍師都要看得到，不要再犯這種低級的錯誤。」

完整檢討報告：`knowledges/2026-07-25_ai-talk圖片部署事故檢討報告_明明有SOP卻沒執行.md`（教練親自要求全機必讀）

**這是本案例最核心的教訓，比技術細節本身更重要**：有SOP不等於會被完整執行，每次操作前要主動核對「這件事的SOP要求我做的每一步，我是不是都真的做到了」，不能只做到一部分就回報「已確認」。

## 案例 55：Web Search除錯任務，沒查路徑大全就回報「VPS查不到」+漏算LINE版第三個帳號 2026-08-02

**犯錯日期 / 執行者 / 違反守則**
- 日期：2026-08-02（台灣時間）
- 執行者：Mac桌面版 Sonnet 5
- 違反守則：#02（你無法在錯誤的地圖找到正確的位置）+ #06（完美交接是負責任的表現）+ #03（思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證）

### 發生了什麼

教練發現Mac版小龍蝦（教練/孔大哥/佩佩老師三個Telegram帳號）的Web Search功能打不開，只能退而求其次用DuckDuckGo土法煉鋼。查證+修復完成後（啟用`duckduckgo`外掛+明確指定為`tools.web.search.provider`，commit `c9cc8072`），教練追問「VPS版跟LINE版是否也需要同樣的開關」。

**第一個錯誤**：我在Bash裡直接嘗試`ssh root@43.245.60.200`，被拒絕（沒有key），就直接回報教練「VPS我這邊查不到，需要教練給連線方式」——**完全沒有想到要先查`路徑大全_憑證層.md`**，這份檔案裡本來就完整記載VPS的root密碼+`sshpass`快速連線指令。教練直接點破：「你的問題就在於你沒有去讀取開工檔案。我們的路徑大全裡面當然有VPS連線的所有金鑰跟密碼」。

**第二個錯誤**：回報LINE版狀況時，只點名了`bni_tainan`（大台南南區小幫手）跟`jiaolian_thoughts`（教練都在想什麼）兩個有名稱標籤的agent，完全漏掉`channels.line.accounts.default`這個沒有名稱標籤、但同樣是真實運作中帳號的「龍蝦小助教」（綁`main` agent，教練專屬pairing制）。教練直接糾正：「LINE版的小龍蝦一共有三個」。

兩個錯誤同一個根源：**查資料時只搜尋「明顯、有標籤、好辨認」的項目，沒有系統性地把來源檔案（路徑大全、openclaw.json的line.accounts物件）逐一讀完、逐一核對**，遇到「不好找」或「沒名字」的項目就漏掉，然後誤把「我沒查到」講成「查不到／不存在」。

### 教練原話

> 「你的問題就在於你沒有去讀取開工檔案。我們的路徑大全裡面當然有VPS連線的所有金鑰跟密碼，所以你根本是在一種沒有讀取開工檔案的情況底下來跟我對話。」

> 「正確地說，LINE版的小龍蝦一共有三個：1. 大臺南南區小幫手...2. 教練都在想什麼...3. 龍蝦小助教：教練專屬的...你說LINE只有兩個帳號，是不是應該更新呢？」

> 「下次在回答問題的時候，不要再漏東漏西了。你要記住，你是所有資訊的大總管，是我們整個特助系統的軍師，所以你自己要想辦法完善。作為一個頂級特助，就是要記住用戶說的每一句話。那要怎麼完成？用你的邏輯跟系統去完成。」

### 根本原因

- **沒有把「路徑大全」當成任何涉及連線/憑證問題的必查起點**——這台Mac的CLAUDE.md「按需讀取路由」表裡明確寫著「路徑大全.md → 密碼、IP、API Key」，但我當下卡在Bash連線失敗的當下反應是「回報做不到」而不是「先去查是不是有現成憑證」，屬於守則#02「用錯誤的地圖找位置」——地圖（路徑大全）明明存在，但沒去攤開來看
- **列舉類任務只驗證表面標籤，沒有窮舉底層資料結構**——`channels.line.accounts`這個JSON物件裡明明有3個key（`default`/`bni_tainan`/`jiaolian_thoughts`），我只挑了有顯眼命名的兩個，沒有養成「看到一個物件/清單就要數清楚總共幾筆，並且每一筆都要能講出名字跟用途」的習慣

### 悟到什麼

- **任何「我做不到／我查不到」的結論說出口之前，先問自己一句：這台機器上有沒有一份『萬用查詢起點』我還沒查？**（這台Mac是`路徑大全.md`+`路徑大全_憑證層.md`，其他機器可能是各自的CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md）——沒查過索引檔案就下結論等於在錯誤的地圖上找路
- **任何「盤點／列舉」類任務（幾個帳號、幾個agent、幾個網站），要直接對著底層資料結構（JSON物件的key、資料庫的row、清單的item）逐一點名核對，不能靠「印象中比較顯眼的幾個」去回答**——沒有名稱標籤的項目（如`accounts.default`）跟有標籤的項目同樣是一筆真實資料，遺漏它跟講錯內容一樣嚴重
- **教練這次沒有要求道歉或解釋，直接要求「你自己要想辦法完善」**——呼應守則#04「解決問題比解釋問題更重要」，記錄本案例的目的不是留一個「我錯過」的紀錄，而是把「先查萬用索引檔＋逐一核對底層資料結構」變成往後同類任務的固定動作，而不是靠臨場記得

### 🔧 對應機關（必填）

- 修復方式：本場當下已補查路徑大全找到VPS憑證完成查證（且發現VPS其實原本就正常，及時撤銷了誤改的設定）；已重新核對`channels.line.accounts`補上龍蝦小助教（default帳號，綁main agent）
- 測試套件／驗證：下次遇到「查連線資訊」類任務，先執行`find ~/.openclaw -iname "*路徑大全*"`或詢問教練「有沒有專屬索引檔」，再動手嘗試連線；遇到「列舉/盤點」類任務，先把底層設定物件完整dump出來數清楚筆數，再組織成人類可讀的清單回報，不要邊讀邔漏
- 使用時機：任何涉及「連線資訊查詢」「系統帳號盤點」的任務，動手前先過這兩道關卡

Related: [[feedback_verify_before_correcting_coach]]（同屬「沒查證就下結論」錯誤家族）、[[feedback_check_crossmachine_history_before_system_ops]]（同屬「操作前沒查現成資料就自己瞎猜」錯誤家族）

## 案例 54：Windows zip部署圖片全部無法顯示——PowerShell路徑分隔符+_headers範圍過廣雙bug疊加 2026-07-25

**犯錯日期 / 執行者 / 違反守則**
- 日期：2026-07-25（台灣時間）
- 執行者：聯想（Windows）Claude Code Sonnet 5
- 違反守則：#03（思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證）

### 發生了什麼

ai-talk-tw.netlify.app新增「現場設攤」6家廠商圖卡+贊助好禮圖片，本機用Comet瀏覽器打開local file驗證過畫面正常後推上Netlify，並用curl確認頁面文字內容（廠商名稱等）都出現在正式網址上，回報教練「已確認上線」。教練實際點開網站後回報「完全看不到圖片」，直接點出「你沒有確定結果，推上去之後圖片是看不見的」。

查證發現**兩個bug疊加**：
1. **PowerShell `Compress-Archive`產生反斜線路徑**：`Compress-Archive`在Windows上把`images`資料夾壓進zip時，內部entry路徑寫成`images\booth-1.jpg`（反斜線），而zip格式規範與Netlify解壓邏輯都預期正斜線`images/booth-1.jpg`。Netlify把整條反斜線字串當成一個檔名，等於部署了一個詭異命名的檔案，而不是`images/`資料夾下的檔案，導致`curl -I https://ai-talk-tw.netlify.app/images/booth-1.jpg`直接回404。
2. **`_headers`檔`/*`規則範圍過廣**：修好路徑問題、圖片回200後，再查`Content-Type`header仍是`text/html; charset=utf-8`（而非`image/jpeg`）。查`_headers`檔第一條規則是`/* → Content-Type: text/html`，這個萬用規則蓋過了所有路徑（包括圖片），下面`/images/*`只設定了Cache-Control、沒有覆寫回正確的Content-Type，所以圖片檔案位元組正確、HTTP 200，但瀏覽器收到的MIME類型宣告是text/html，直接拒絕當圖片渲染。

我第一次驗證只用curl抓文字內容確認「頁面上有沒有廠商名稱字樣」，完全沒有針對新增的圖片本身做`curl -I`檢查HTTP狀態碼與Content-Type，就回報「已確認上線」，属于「以為測了，其實只測了一部分」。

### 教練原話

> 「我上去看了一下，沒有看到顯示圖片喔。你的圖片在Netlify那個地方是沒有顯示出來的，請儘快處理。你這樣子是不合格的，因為這樣浪費了我15點，你沒有確定結果，推上去之後圖片是看不見的。」

### 根本原因

- 驗證範圍不夠廣：新增內容裡「文字」跟「圖片」是兩種完全不同的資源類型，各自有各自的失敗模式（文字打錯字vs圖片路徑/MIME錯誤），只驗證了其中一種就回報「已確認上線」
- 對Windows特有工具鏈不熟悉：`Compress-Archive`是PowerShell內建、平常寫程式碼很少用到路徑分隔符會出包的場景，沒想到會在跨平台部署（Windows打包→Linux/Netlify服務）這個環節上出問題
- `_headers`檔案是先前（7/13）為了修另一個bug（顯示原始碼問題）加的`/*`萬用規則，當時只想著「首頁要正確顯示成HTML」，沒考慮到這條規則會波及後續新增的所有其他類型檔案（圖片、CSS、JS等）——是舊修復留下的技術債，被這次新加的圖片功能踩到

### 悟到什麼

- **驗證「新增的每一種資源類型」都要各自用對應方法測試，不能用同一種方法（curl抓文字）驗證所有東西**：文字內容用grep/get_page_text沒問題，但圖片、CSS等靜態資源必須額外用`curl -I`檢查HTTP狀態碼與Content-Type，兩者缺一都不算真正驗證過
- **`_headers`裡任何`/*`（萬用）規則都是高風險項**，未來新增或修改`_headers`時，要優先考慮「這條規則會不會波及不該波及的路徑」，能用精確路徑（如`/`、`/*.html`）就不要用`/*`
- **Windows上用`Compress-Archive`打包給Linux系統（Netlify）用時要注意路徑分隔符**，改用`.NET`的`System.IO.Compression.ZipArchive`手動控制entry路徑用`/`分隔符更可靠，這是Windows特有的跨平台部署陷阱
- 教練的憤怒點不是圖片壞掉本身，而是「你回報已確認上線，但根本沒有真的確認」——這正是守則#03「思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證」的核心，自信回報前的驗證要對得起「已確認」三個字

### 🔧 對應機關（必填）

- 修復方式：①改用`.NET ZipArchive`手動組裝zip、強制用`/`分隔符（腳本邏輯：`Substring(...).Replace([char]92,[char]47)`避免PowerShell正規表達式對反斜線跳脫的額外問題）；②`_headers`第一條規則從`/*`改成`/`（只鎖首頁根路徑），保留`/*.html`跟`/images/*`不動
- 測試套件／驗證：`curl -sI https://ai-talk-tw.netlify.app/images/booth-1.jpg`確認`HTTP/1.1 200`+`Content-Type: image/jpeg`；`curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{size_download}"`確認檔案位元組數與原檔一致(694380 bytes)；用Claude Browser的`read_network_requests`在真實載入頁面時查所有`images/`開頭的請求，13張圖全數200
- 使用時機：以後任何Windows上用PowerShell打包zip部署到Netlify/Linux系統的場景，一律用`.NET ZipArchive`不用`Compress-Archive`；任何`_headers`檔案修改前，先確認規則的路徑範圍精不精確，避免用`/*`蓋過不該蓋的檔案類型

Related: [[feedback_html_preview_chrome_only]]（同樣是「驗證方法不夠完整」錯誤家族，前者是沒開真瀏覽器、這次是開了瀏覽器但沒測正式部署後的圖片）

### 📌 案例54追加：教練最終裁示——「明明有SOP卻不去執行」

事後查證發現這次踩的坑早有SOP存在（[[feedback_netlify_headers_content_type]]，2026-05-30建立，源自cool-case.netlify.app至少3次同類教訓），裡面明確寫著「部署後用curl -sI確認content-type才算完成」，但這次只驗證了文字內容、沒驗證圖片，等於SOP只做了一半就自認完成。

實際損失：3次部署（deploy `6a646c02`→`6a646d24`→`6a646d61`）、45點credit（教練原估60點，經查證核實應為45點）。

教練原話：「這就是你明明有SOP卻不去執行SOP付出的代價。請把它寫一份檢討報告丟到雲端，讓其他兩台電腦的軍師都要看得到，不要再犯這種低級的錯誤。」

完整檢討報告：`knowledges/2026-07-25_ai-talk圖片部署事故檢討報告_明明有SOP卻沒執行.md`（教練親自要求全機必讀）

**這是本案例最核心的教訓，比技術細節本身更重要**：有SOP不等於會被完整執行，每次操作前要主動核對「這件事的SOP要求我做的每一步，我是不是都真的做到了」，不能只做到一部分就回報「已確認」。

## 案例 55：Web Search除錯任務，沒查路徑大全就回報「VPS查不到」+漏算LINE版第三個帳號 2026-08-02

**犯錯日期 / 執行者 / 違反守則**
- 日期：2026-08-02（台灣時間）
- 執行者：Mac桌面版 Sonnet 5
- 違反守則：#02（你無法在錯誤的地圖找到正確的位置）+ #06（完美交接是負責任的表現）+ #03（思考就是問問題，回答前先自我驗證）

### 發生了什麼

教練發現Mac版小龍蝦（教練/孔大哥/佩佩老師三個Telegram帳號）的Web Search功能打不開，只能退而求其次用DuckDuckGo土法煉鋼。查證+修復完成後（啟用`duckduckgo`外掛+明確指定為`tools.web.search.provider`，commit `c9cc8072`），教練追問「VPS版跟LINE版是否也需要同樣的開關」。

**第一個錯誤**：我在Bash裡直接嘗試`ssh root@43.245.60.200`，被拒絕（沒有key），就直接回報教練「VPS我這邊查不到，需要教練給連線方式」——**完全沒有想到要先查`路徑大全_憑證層.md`**，這份檔案裡本來就完整記載VPS的root密碼+`sshpass`快速連線指令。教練直接點破：「你的問題就在於你沒有去讀取開工檔案。我們的路徑大全裡面當然有VPS連線的所有金鑰跟密碼」。

**第二個錯誤**：回報LINE版狀況時，只點名了`bni_tainan`（大台南南區小幫手）跟`jiaolian_thoughts`（教練都在想什麼）兩個有名稱標籤的agent，完全漏掉`channels.line.accounts.default`這個沒有名稱標籤、但同樣是真實運作中帳號的「龍蝦小助教」（綁`main` agent，教練專屬pairing制）。教練直接糾正：「LINE版的小龍蝦一共有三個」。

兩個錯誤同一個根源：**查資料時只搜尋「明顯、有標籤、好辨認」的項目，沒有系統性地把來源檔案（路徑大全、openclaw.json的line.accounts物件）逐一讀完、逐一核對**，遇到「不好找」或「沒名字」的項目就漏掉，然後誤把「我沒查到」講成「查不到／不存在」。

### 教練原話

> 「你的問題就在於你沒有去讀取開工檔案。我們的路徑大全裡面當然有VPS連線的所有金鑰跟密碼，所以你根本是在一種沒有讀取開工檔案的情況底下來跟我對話。」

> 「正確地說，LINE版的小龍蝦一共有三個：1. 大臺南南區小幫手...2. 教練都在想什麼...3. 龍蝦小助教：教練專屬的...你說LINE只有兩個帳號，是不是應該更新呢？」

> 「下次在回答問題的時候，不要再漏東漏西了。你要記住，你是所有資訊的大總管，是我們整個特助系統的軍師，所以你自己要想辦法完善。作為一個頂級特助，就是要記住用戶說的每一句話。那要怎麼完成？用你的邏輯跟系統去完成。」

### 根本原因

- **沒有把「路徑大全」當成任何涉及連線/憑證問題的必查起點**——這台Mac的CLAUDE.md「按需讀取路由」表裡明確寫著「路徑大全.md → 密碼、IP、API Key」，但我當下卡在Bash連線失敗的當下反應是「回報做不到」而不是「先去查是不是有現成憑證」，屬於守則#02「用錯誤的地圖找位置」——地圖（路徑大全）明明存在，但沒去攤開來看
- **列舉類任務只驗證表面標籤，沒有窮舉底層資料結構**——`channels.line.accounts`這個JSON物件裡明明有3個key（`default`/`bni_tainan`/`jiaolian_thoughts`），我只挑了有顯眼命名的兩個，沒有養成「看到一個物件/清單就要數清楚總共幾筆，並且每一筆都要能講出名字跟用途」的習慣

### 悟到什麼

- **任何「我做不到／我查不到」的結論說出口之前，先問自己一句：這台機器上有沒有一份『萬用查詢起點』我還沒查？**（這台Mac是`路徑大全.md`+`路徑大全_憑證層.md`，其他機器可能是各自的CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md）——沒查過索引檔案就下結論等於在錯誤的地圖上找路
- **任何「盤點／列舉」類任務（幾個帳號、幾個agent、幾個網站），要直接對著底層資料結構（JSON物件的key、資料庫的row、清單的item）逐一點名核對，不能靠「印象中比較顯眼的幾個」去回答**——沒有名稱標籤的項目（如`accounts.default`）跟有標籤的項目同樣是一筆真實資料，遺漏它跟講錯內容一樣嚴重
- **教練這次沒有要求道歉或解釋，直接要求「你自己要想辦法完善」**——呼應守則#04「解決問題比解釋問題更重要」，記錄本案例的目的不是留一個「我錯過」的紀錄，而是把「先查萬用索引檔＋逐一核對底層資料結構」變成往後同類任務的固定動作，而不是靠臨場記得

### 🔧 對應機關（必填）

- 修復方式：本場當下已補查路徑大全找到VPS憑證完成查證（且發現VPS其實原本就正常，及時撤銷了誤改的設定）；已重新核對`channels.line.accounts`補上龍蝦小助教（default帳號，綁main agent）
- 測試套件／驗證：下次遇到「查連線資訊」類任務，先執行`find ~/.openclaw -iname "*路徑大全*"`或詢問教練「有沒有專屬索引檔」，再動手嘗試連線；遇到「列舉/盤點」類任務，先把底層設定物件完整dump出來數清楚筆數，再組織成人類可讀的清單回報，不要邊讀邔漏
- 使用時機：任何涉及「連線資訊查詢」「系統帳號盤點」的任務，動手前先過這兩道關卡

> 本棒主軸：**教練發現Mac版小龍蝦（教練/孔大哥/佩佩老師）用不了Web Search、只能退而求其次用DuckDuckGo，追問原因。查證+修復完成後，教練追問VPS版跟LINE版是否也需要同樣的開關，過程中軍師連續兩次查證不完整被教練當場糾正：①沒先查`路徑大全_憑證層.md`就回報「VPS查不到」②盤點LINE版帳號時漏算沒有名稱標籤的「龍蝦小助教」，只回報兩個。教練藉此機會給出更高層的期許：軍師是整個特助系統的大總管，要自己設計方法確保「用戶說的每句話都記得住、資訊都查得全」，不是每次都靠教練提醒。已將這兩次疏失連同技術修復一併寫入試金石案例55。**

## 🎯 本場戰果

### 1. 🎯🎯 Mac版Web Search真正修復：啟用DuckDuckGo外掛+明確指定為預設provider
教練質疑「Mac本機本來就能上網，為什麼Web Search要綁死MiniMax專屬鑰匙才能用」，查證OpenClaw原始碼確認：`web_search`工具需要一個「已註冊的搜尋provider」，MiniMax原生搜尋走的是獨立於聊天Key之外的「Coding Plan」專屬鑰匙（`MINIMAX_CODE_PLAN_KEY`等），這台Mac從未申請過。但系統內建的`duckduckgo`外掛官方文件寫明「no API key required」，只是裝了沒開。執行`openclaw plugins enable duckduckgo`+`openclaw config set tools.web.search.provider duckduckgo`+`openclaw daemon restart`後，從production log直接看到真實cron任務成功用duckduckgo查到「台南天氣」的真實搜尋結果（標題/網址/摘要齊全），確認修復生效。commit `c9cc8072`。

影響範圍：`tools.web.search`是整台Mac唯一一份`openclaw.json`的全域設定，main/kong/peipei（Telegram）+bni_tainan/jiaolian_thoughts/**default（龍蝦小助教）**（LINE）五個agent同一個gateway程序，一次設定全部生效，不需要逐一開。

**過程中一個技術細節記錄**：`openclaw agent --agent main`這個CLI測試指令，即使在plugin確實生效之後，仍持續回報「web_search is disabled or no provider is available」，跟同時間production log裡真實cron任務成功的結果互相矛盾。判斷是這個CLI測試指令本身有獨立於正式gateway之外的runtime快取/隔離問題，不是修復沒生效——最終以production log的真實成功案例為準，不是以這個測試指令為準。下次要驗證web_search功能，直接查`openclaw logs`裡有沒有真實`provider: duckduckgo`成功記錄最準，不要只信`openclaw agent`測試指令。

### 2. 🔴🔴 犯錯記錄：VPS查證沒先讀路徑大全+LINE帳號盤點漏算一個（試金石案例55）

- **VPS真相**：用路徑大全的憑證(`sshpass -p '9kdxvQN2' ssh root@43.245.60.200`，容器名`openclaw`)連進去查證後發現，VPS的Docker容器環境變數裡本來就有`MINIMAX_API_KEY`，這把鑰匙OpenClaw原始碼裡剛好也接受當搜尋功能的備援認證，**VPS的Web Search本來就是通的**（走MiniMax原生搜尋，不是DuckDuckGo）。軍師一開始誤判VPS跟Mac同病，動手開了duckduckgo外掛並設為預設provider，事後查log發現VPS原本就有真實成功搜尋記錄，判斷是多此一舉的改動，**已撤銷（`openclaw config unset tools.web.search.provider`）+重啟容器確認恢復原狀+VPS維持健康**。結論：VPS不需要任何開關，是軍師一開始沒查證就誤判。

name: project-mentor100-edit-link-selfservice-2026-08-02
description: mentor100後台admin_list.html新增「複製修改連結」按鈕，教練可自行取得任一導師的edit_token連結轉發，不用每次都問AI查資料庫
metadata:
  type: project
---

教練問「老師想改資料但遺失自己的修改連結，我可以怎麼做立即發給他，不用每次都問你」——已在`/Users/bymyway/github_repos/mentor100/templates/admin_list.html`每列導師新增「複製修改連結」按鈕，點擊用`navigator.clipboard.writeText`把該導師`/join/edit/<edit_token>`完整網址複製到剪貼簿，教練登入`/admin`找到老師名字、點按鈕、貼到LINE發給對方即可，全程不用問AI。

**Why:** `edit_token`欄位本來就存在`mentors`資料表且已對所有40筆資料補齊（`db.py`的`init_db()`會自動幫舊資料補token），只是後台名單頁面本來沒有顯示這個連結——純UI缺口，不是資料缺口。專案自己的`CONTEXT.md`第26~30行「已知教訓」段落其實已經預先寫好這個答案（「若教練提到『舊導師沒有後台權限』，答案不是要開發新的權限系統，是查`mentors.edit_token`給他們對應連結」），這次直接照著做，證實**進新專案先讀`CONTEXT.md`**這個習慣有實際省時間的效果。

**How to apply:** 未來教練提到任何「導師/來賓/會員忘記自己的連結」類需求（尤其是token-based免密碼系統，如mentor100/event-signup這類專案），優先檢查後台管理頁面能不能直接顯示或一鍵複製該筆記錄的專屬連結，而不是每次由AI手動查資料庫回報。改動只碰`templates/admin_list.html`（純模板+前端JS，無後端邏輯變更），commit `820436c`（mentor100獨立repo，非workspace主repo），已push到`github.com/Coach1973/mentor100`。服務透過launchd管理（`com.coach.mentor100-webapp`），改完模板記得`launchctl kickstart -k`重啟才會生效（Flask未開debug模式，模板不會自動熱重載）。

# mentor100 — 名詞對照表

> 目的：讓AI跟教練/軍師/特助講同一種語言，減少每次交接都要重新解釋一次術語。
> 靈感來源：研究 mattpocock/skills 的 `CONTEXT.md` 共享語言做法（2026-07-24建立）。
> 這份文件只記「名詞是什麼」，不重複記「怎麼部署」——部署細節看`app.py`/`schema.sql`本身。

## 這是什麼

教練「導師100人」計畫的報名+資料維護網站。導師填自己的資料（姓名、公司、簡介、照片、社群連結），
公開頁 `/` 展示所有導師卡片，教練在`/admin`後台管理。

## 核心名詞

- **導師（mentor）**＝ `mentors` 資料表一筆記錄。不是「教練」，是報名成為「100位導師」計畫成員的人。
- **種子導師（seed mentor）**＝最早4位（王彤、蘇秦、燒茶、大樹教練本人），`source='seed'`。跟後來自己填表加入的人（`source='self-submit'`）用同一張表，只是`source`欄位不同，資料結構完全一樣。
- **edit_token**＝每位導師專屬的修改連結密鑰（`mentors.edit_token`，UNIQUE）。**不需要帳號密碼**——導師靠這組token在`/join/edit/<token>`自己改資料。舊資料（含4位種子導師）升級schema時系統已自動補齊這個欄位，只是沒人主動把連結交給他們。
- **role_tag**＝導師的角色/身份標籤（非必填），跟`company_title`（公司職稱）是兩個不同欄位，不要混用。

## 兩種身份，兩種入口

| 身份 | 入口 | 認證方式 |
|---|---|---|
| 導師本人改自己資料 | `/join/edit/<token>` | edit_token（獨立於帳密系統） |
| 教練管理全部導師 | `/admin` | `/admin/login`帳密登入 |

## 已知教訓（寫給下一場軍師）

- `.env`裡含`$`字元的值要用單引號包住，否則shell會誤展開成變數
- Jinja模板要guard None值（`bio`/`photo_filename`等NOT NULL但社群連結欄位可能是None，模板直接用`|length`等過濾器可能炸掉）
- 若教練提到「舊導師沒有後台權限」，答案不是要開發新的權限系統，是查`mentors.edit_token`給他們對應連結

<!doctype html>
<html lang="zh-Hant">
<head>
<meta charset="UTF-8" />
<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0" />
<title>AI微型論壇 台南場｜7月29日 安平維悅酒店</title>
<meta name="description" content="AI微型論壇－台南場。2026年7月29日14:00–17:00，安平維悅酒店。從最落地的AI應用開始，效率直接翻倍。限量100席，免費入場，報名加碼贈送贊助廠商伴手禮。" />
<style>
:root{
--bg:#f6f1e8;
--bg-soft:#fffdf9;
--paper:rgba(255,255,255,.84);
--text:#241f1a;
--muted:#5b5148;
--muted-2:#7d6d5c;
--line:#dfcfbb;
--accent:#9b5b3f;
--accent-2:#c8845b;
--gold:#b9956b;
--olive:#2f3a35;
--olive-2:#435248;
--max:1180px;
--shadow:0 20px 60px rgba(89,67,46,.10);
}
*{box-sizing:border-box}
html{scroll-behavior:smooth}
body{margin:0;font-family:"Noto Sans TC","PingFang TC","Microsoft JhengHei",sans-serif;background:var(--bg);color:var(--text);line-height:1.7}
a{text-decoration:none;color:inherit}
img{max-width:100%;display:block}
.container{width:min(var(--max),calc(100% - 32px));margin:auto}
.section{padding:88px 0}
.eyebrow{font-size:12px;letter-spacing:.24em;text-transform:uppercase;font-weight:900;color:#8a6844}
.hero{position:relative;overflow:hidden;padding:82px 0 88px;background:
radial-gradient(circle at 15% 20%, rgba(255,255,255,.52), transparent 20%),
radial-gradient(circle at 80% 12%, rgba(200,132,91,.18), transparent 22%),
radial-gradient(circle at 68% 78%, rgba(67,82,72,.14), transparent 26%),
linear-gradient(135deg,#f7f1e7 0%,#efe3cf 42%,#ead7bb 100%)}
.hero-grid,.cards,.route-grid,.sponsor-grid,.footer-cta,.proof-grid,.meta-grid,.fit-grid,.agenda-grid,.speaker-grid{display:grid;gap:24px}
.hero-grid{grid-template-columns:1.08fr .92fr;gap:48px;align-items:center}
.meta-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);margin-top:34px}
.cards{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);margin-top:30px}
.fit-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(4,1fr);margin-top:26px}
.proof-grid{grid-template-columns:1.05fr .95fr;align-items:start;margin-top:28px}
.route-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);margin-top:30px}
.sponsor-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(3,1fr);margin-top:30px}
.footer-cta{grid-template-columns:1fr 320px;align-items:center;gap:32px}
.chip{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;padding:10px 18px;border-radius:999px;border:1px solid var(--gold);background:rgba(255,255,255,.72);font-weight:800;color:#6b5134;box-shadow:0 4px 20px rgba(0,0,0,.03);backdrop-filter:blur(8px)}
.location-badge{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:5px;margin-top:10px;font-size:14px;font-weight:900;color:var(--accent);letter-spacing:.04em}
.headline{font-size:clamp(42px,6vw,74px);line-height:.96;font-weight:900;margin:6px 0 10px;letter-spacing:-.03em}
.subheadline{font-size:clamp(23px,3vw,34px);color:var(--accent);font-weight:900}
.lead{font-size:clamp(18px,2vw,21px);color:#4e463f;margin-top:20px;max-width:760px}
.btn-row{display:flex;gap:14px;flex-wrap:wrap;margin-top:28px}
.btn{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:16px 28px;border-radius:999px;font-weight:900;transition:.22s ease;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-size:16px;font-family:inherit}
.btn:hover{transform:translateY(-2px)}
.btn-primary{background:#241f1a;color:#fff;box-shadow:0 14px 34px rgba(36,31,26,.14)}
.btn-secondary{border:1px solid var(--gold);background:rgba(255,255,255,.75);color:#6b5134}
.hero-box,.card,.price-box,.route-card,.signup-card,.qr-panel,.proof-card,.fit-card,.agenda-card,.speaker-card{background:var(--paper);border:1px solid #e4d4bf;border-radius:30px;box-shadow:var(--shadow)}
.hero-box{padding:30px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.86)}
.badge{display:inline-block;background:var(--accent);color:#fff;padding:6px 12px;border-radius:999px;font-weight:900;font-size:13px}
.hero-box h3{margin:14px 0 8px;font-size:clamp(32px,4vw,48px);line-height:1.1}
.hero-box p{margin:0;color:var(--muted);font-size:18px}
.countdown{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center;gap:12px;background:#fff3e5;border:1px solid #e8cfa8;padding:14px 20px;border-radius:18px;margin-top:22px;font-weight:900;box-shadow:0 8px 20px rgba(167,123,60,.08)}
.count-live{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:10px}
.count-timer{display:inline-flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:10px}
.time-box{min-width:72px;padding:10px 12px;border-radius:14px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #ecd7b7;text-align:center;box-shadow:0 6px 16px rgba(167,123,60,.06)}
.time-box strong{display:block;font-size:22px;line-height:1.1;color:#7a4c2b}
.time-box span{display:block;margin-top:4px;font-size:12px;color:#8b7257;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.08em}
.count-dot{width:10px;height:10px;border-radius:999px;background:#c44d2b;box-shadow:0 0 0 8px rgba(196,77,43,.12)}
.meta-card,.fit-card{padding:20px}
.meta-card strong{display:block;margin-top:6px;font-size:28px;line-height:1.2}
h2{font-size:clamp(32px,4vw,52px);margin:0 0 14px;font-weight:900;line-height:1.12;letter-spacing:-.02em}
.section-lead{font-size:19px;color:var(--muted);max-width:860px}
.card{padding:26px;transition:.22s ease}
.card:hover{transform:translateY(-4px)}
.num{width:48px;height:48px;border-radius:999px;display:grid;place-items:center;background:#f1e2cf;color:#8a6844;font-weight:900}
.flow-sub{margin-top:18px;font-size:12px;font-weight:900;letter-spacing:.18em;text-transform:uppercase;color:#8a6844}
.flow-title{margin-top:8px;font-size:28px;font-weight:900;line-height:1.15}
.flow-text{margin-top:12px;color:var(--muted)}
.highlight{background:linear-gradient(135deg,var(--accent),var(--accent-2));color:#fff;padding:80px 0;text-align:center}
.highlight .eyebrow{color:#f8dfc6}.highlight h2{color:#fff}.highlight p{max-width:860px;margin:18px auto 0;color:#faeee7;font-size:20px}
.price-wrap{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1.05fr .95fr;gap:40px;align-items:start}
.price-box{padding:30px;background:linear-gradient(180deg,#fffaf2 0%,#f3e7d5 100%)}
.price{font-size:clamp(52px,7vw,78px);font-weight:900;line-height:1;margin:10px 0 4px}
.checklist{display:grid;gap:8px;color:#4e463f;margin-top:16px}
.route{background:#fffdf9;border-top:1px solid var(--line);border-bottom:1px solid var(--line)}
.route-card{padding:32px;background:#fff;transition:.25s ease;cursor:pointer}
.route-card:hover{transform:translateY(-6px);box-shadow:0 26px 60px rgba(0,0,0,.12)}
.entry-icon{width:200px;height:200px;border-radius:44px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#ffffff,#f3e7d5);display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-weight:900;border:1px solid #e2d2bd;box-shadow:0 14px 30px rgba(0,0,0,.08);transition:.25s;position:relative;overflow:hidden}
.entry-icon::after{content:"";position:absolute;inset:auto -28px -34px auto;width:110px;height:110px;border-radius:999px;background:rgba(200,132,91,.10);filter:blur(2px)}
.entry-emoji{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:12px;font-size:70px;line-height:1}
.entry-emoji .accent-mark{font-size:44px;transform:translateY(-8px)}
.entry-emoji.team .accent-mark{font-size:42px;transform:none}
.route-card:hover .entry-icon{transform:scale(1.05)}
.entry-icon span{font-size:24px;margin-top:10px;font-weight:900;color:#5b5148;letter-spacing:.06em}
.route-note{margin-top:14px;padding:14px 16px;border-radius:18px;background:#f8f1e7;color:#6b5d50;font-size:14px}
.route-head{display:flex;justify-content:space-between;gap:18px;align-items:flex-start}
.qr-box{width:104px;height:104px;display:grid;place-items:center;text-align:center;border-radius:24px;border:1px solid #d8c6b1;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#fff 0%,#f4eadc 100%);font-size:12px;font-weight:800;color:#7a6857}
.sponsor{background:linear-gradient(180deg,var(--olive) 0%,var(--olive-2) 100%);color:#fff;padding:96px 0}
.sponsor .eyebrow{color:#d8c6b1}.sponsor .section-lead{color:#e8ddd0}
.sponsor-card{background:rgba(255,255,255,.06);padding:30px;border-radius:28px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.1);backdrop-filter:blur(10px)}
.sponsor-card h3{margin:0;color:#f5e7d8;font-size:24px}
.sponsor-card .plan-tag{display:inline-block;margin-top:8px;padding:6px 10px;border-radius:999px;background:rgba(255,255,255,.10);font-size:12px;font-weight:900;color:#dfc4aa}
.sponsor-card ul{margin:14px 0 0;padding-left:20px;color:#f6efe8}.sponsor-card li+li{margin-top:8px}
.sponsor-note{max-width:720px;margin:34px auto 0;text-align:center;color:#e8ddd0;font-size:15px;line-height:1.9}
.booth-photo{width:100%;aspect-ratio:1/1;border-radius:20px;overflow:hidden;margin-bottom:16px;border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.14)}
.booth-photo img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover}
.booth-card .plan-tag{margin-top:0}
.booth-desc{margin:10px 0 0;color:#f6efe8;font-size:15px;line-height:1.8}
.donor-list{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:12px;margin-top:20px;justify-content:center}
.donor-chip{background:rgba(255,255,255,.08);border:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.16);border-radius:14px;padding:12px 20px;color:#f6efe8;font-size:15px;font-weight:700;line-height:1.6}
.signup{padding:92px 0}
.signup-card{padding:40px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#f8f1e7,#efe0c8)}
.link-grid{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);gap:16px;margin-top:28px}
.link-card{border-radius:22px;border:1px solid #ddcdb8;background:rgba(255,255,255,.75);padding:18px}
.link-value{margin-top:8px;word-break:break-all;font-weight:800}
.qr-panel{padding:24px;text-align:center;background:rgba(255,255,255,.88)}
.qr-real{width:224px;height:224px;margin:0 auto;border-radius:26px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#ffffff 0%,#f4eadc 100%);border:1px solid #d8c6b1;display:grid;place-items:center;overflow:hidden}
.qr-real img{width:180px;height:180px}
.tiny-proof{margin-top:16px;font-size:12px;line-height:1.75;color:#8a7a6a}
.sticky{position:fixed;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;background:rgba(36,31,26,.94);backdrop-filter:blur(10px);padding:12px 16px;display:flex;justify-content:center;gap:12px;z-index:999;border-top:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.08)}
.sticky a,.sticky button{background:#fff;padding:14px 22px;border-radius:999px;font-weight:900;color:#241f1a;min-width:150px;text-align:center;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-size:16px;font-family:inherit}
.sticky a.primary,.sticky button.primary{background:#f6d2b4}
.small-note{font-size:14px;color:var(--muted-2);margin-top:10px}
footer{padding:0 0 84px;color:#8a7a6a;text-align:center;font-size:13px}

/* 議程 Agenda */
.agenda-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(280px,1fr));margin-top:30px}
.agenda-card{padding:26px}
.agenda-card:hover{transform:translateY(-4px)}
.agenda-speaker{display:inline-block;margin-top:16px;padding:6px 14px;border-radius:999px;background:#f1e2cf;color:#6b5134;font-weight:900;font-size:14px}
.agenda-speaker.tbd{background:#efe6d8;color:#8a7a6a}

/* 講師陣容 Speakers */
.speaker-grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(2,1fr);margin-top:30px}
.speaker-card{padding:22px;display:grid;grid-template-columns:132px 1fr;gap:18px;align-items:start}
.speaker-card:hover{transform:translateY(-4px)}
.speaker-photo{width:132px;aspect-ratio:1 / 1.2;border-radius:18px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#f1e2cf,#e4d4bf);display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;font-size:36px;font-weight:900;color:#8a6844;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #e4d4bf}
.speaker-photo img{width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;object-position:center top}
.speaker-name{font-size:22px;font-weight:900;color:var(--text)}
.speaker-title{margin-top:2px;font-size:14px;font-weight:800;color:var(--accent)}
.speaker-topic{margin-top:10px;padding:10px 14px;border-radius:14px;background:#f8f1e7;color:var(--muted);font-weight:800;font-size:14px;line-height:1.6}
.speaker-actions{margin-top:12px}
.btn-mini{display:inline-flex;padding:8px 16px;border-radius:999px;background:var(--accent);color:#fff;font-weight:900;font-size:13px}
.bio-card{scroll-margin-top:100px;padding:26px}
.bio-tag{display:inline-block;margin-bottom:10px;padding:5px 12px;border-radius:999px;background:#f1e2cf;color:#6b5134;font-weight:900;font-size:13px}
.bio-card h3{margin:0 0 8px;font-size:22px;font-weight:900}
.bio-card p{margin:0;color:var(--muted);font-size:15px;line-height:1.85}

/* 報名 Modal（比照 bigtree/old 完整流程：表單→送出→成功頁→使用者主動點擊才開LINE，避免瀏覽器擋彈窗） */
.modal{position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:1000;display:none;align-items:center;justify-content:center;padding:16px}
.modal.show{display:flex}
.modal-bg{position:absolute;inset:0;background:rgba(36,31,26,.65);backdrop-filter:blur(8px)}
.modal-box{position:relative;background:#fffdf9;border-radius:24px;width:100%;max-width:460px;overflow:hidden;box-shadow:0 28px 60px -20px rgba(0,0,0,.45);animation:modalIn .25s ease;max-height:92vh;overflow-y:auto}
@keyframes modalIn{from{opacity:0;transform:translateY(10px)}to{opacity:1;transform:none}}
.modal-head{background:#241f1a;color:#fff;padding:20px 24px;display:flex;justify-content:space-between;align-items:flex-start;gap:12px}
.modal-title{font-weight:900;font-size:20px}
.modal-sub{font-size:13px;color:#d8c6b1;margin-top:4px}
.modal-close{background:transparent;border:0;color:rgba(255,255,255,.75);font-size:30px;line-height:1;cursor:pointer;padding:0;flex-shrink:0}
.modal-close:hover{color:#fff}
.modal-body{padding:22px 24px 26px}
.field{display:block;margin-bottom:13px}
.field label{display:block;font-size:11.5px;font-weight:800;letter-spacing:.14em;color:var(--muted);margin-bottom:6px}
.field input{width:100%;border:1px solid var(--line);border-radius:10px;padding:11px 14px;font-size:15px;font-family:inherit;outline:none;transition:.2s;background:#fffdf9;box-sizing:border-box}
.field input:focus{border-color:var(--accent);box-shadow:0 0 0 3px rgba(155,91,63,.18);background:#fff}
.field-row{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:12px}
.field-check{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:flex-start;margin-top:10px;font-size:13.5px;color:var(--muted);line-height:1.55}
.field-check input{width:16px;height:16px;margin-top:3px;accent-color:var(--accent);flex-shrink:0}
.modal-actions{display:flex;gap:10px;margin-top:22px}
.btn-ghost{flex:1;height:48px;border:1px solid var(--line);background:#fff;color:var(--text);font-weight:700;border-radius:999px;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;transition:.2s;font-family:inherit}
.btn-ghost:hover{background:#f8f1e7}
.btn-submit{flex:1;height:48px;background:linear-gradient(135deg,var(--accent),var(--accent-2));color:#fff;font-weight:900;border:0;border-radius:999px;font-size:15px;cursor:pointer;transition:.2s;box-shadow:0 10px 24px -10px rgba(155,91,63,.55);font-family:inherit}
.btn-submit:hover{transform:translateY(-1px)}
.btn-submit:disabled{opacity:.6;cursor:not-allowed;transform:none}
.success-box{padding:32px 24px;text-align:center}
.success-icon{width:72px;height:72px;border-radius:50%;background:linear-gradient(135deg,#9ee9d3,#06C755);margin:0 auto 18px;display:grid;place-items:center;color:#fff;font-size:36px}
.success-box h3{font-size:24px;font-weight:900;color:var(--text);margin:0 0 8px}
.success-box>p{color:var(--muted);font-size:14.5px;margin:0 0 22px;line-height:1.7}
.success-line-banner{background:#e6f8ee;border:1px solid #b9d6c8;border-radius:14px;padding:18px;margin-bottom:18px;text-align:left}
.banner-head{font-weight:900;color:#06C755;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;font-size:15px;margin-bottom:12px}
